## Document format conversion

Use Pandoc for document conversion and `pptx2md` to extract slide content into Quarto Markdown. The Docker examples assume a local image named `pandoc_dockerfile` that contains Pandoc.

### Word to Markdown

Run this command in the directory containing `input.docx`. The converted file is written as `output.md` in that directory:

```sh
docker run --rm \
  --volume "$PWD:/data" \
  --workdir /data \
  pandoc_dockerfile \
  input.docx --from=docx --to=markdown --wrap=none --output=output.md
```

### Markdown to Word

The user and group options make the generated file owned by the current host user:

```sh
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  --volume "$PWD:/data" \
  --workdir /data \
  pandoc_dockerfile \
  input.md --from=markdown --to=docx --output=output.docx
```

### PowerPoint to Quarto Markdown

Install `pptx2md` in an appropriate Python environment, then run it with the presentation in the current directory. The command extracts slide content and notes and places extracted images in `images/`:

```sh
pptx2md "slides.pptx" \
  --output "slides_with_notes.qmd" \
  --enable-slides \
  --qmd \
  --image-dir "images"
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Prompt to polish extracted slides" collapse="true"}

After extraction, this prompt can be used with a language model to reformat the content for Reveal.js slides in Quarto while preserving its meaning:

```text
You are a formatter for Reveal.js / Quarto slides.

Task: Convert the input into plain Markdown suitable for Reveal.js with Quarto.

Rules:
- Keep the existing YAML header exactly as it is.
- Remove ALL HTML tags and inline CSS (e.g., <div>, <h3>, <ul>, <li>, <p>, style=...).
- Preserve the slide structure:
  - Keep slide titles as "## ...".
- Ensure there is a blank newline before every list.
- Convert lists to Markdown bullets ("- ...").
- Convert quoted statements into Markdown blockquotes ("> ...").
- Put all sources / attributions into a Quarto aside block in this exact form:

  ::: aside
  — Source
  :::

- Actively remove all figure captions.
- Do NOT add new content and do NOT remove semantic content; only reformat.

Image and layout rules (apply automatically):
- If a slide contains one image only, format it as:

  `![](path){fig-align="center" width="50%"}`

- If a slide contains two images only, place them in a two-column layout:

  ::: columns
  ::: column
  ![](path1)
  :::
  ::: column
  ![](path2)
  :::
  :::

- If a slide contains text and one image, place the text in the left column and the image in the right column:

  ::: columns
  ::: column
  [text content]
  :::
  ::: column
  ![](path){width="300px"}
  :::
  :::

- If images are present without explicit widths, use 40% by default, unless overridden by the rules above.
- Preserve existing explicit image widths when they do not conflict with these rules.

- Output ONLY the converted Markdown.
- Do not explain anything.
```

:::

## Bibliographic format conversion

[`bibliography-io`](https://colrev-environment.github.io/bibliography-io/) reads and writes bibliographic records in formats including BibTeX and RIS. It infers the file format from the filename extension. For example, convert an RIS file to BibTeX with:

```sh
uv run --with bibliography-io python - <<'PY'
from bibliography_io import load_raw, write

records = load_raw("references.ris")
write(records, path="references.bib")
PY
```

This example uses the library’s raw I/O API. Inspect converted records for fields that may not map directly between formats. Consult the project’s [format support table](https://colrev-environment.github.io/bibliography-io/usage.html#supported-formats) for current read/write capabilities and optional format dependencies.

## Video conversion

Use FFmpeg to re-encode a video into an MP4 file with H.264 video and AAC audio:

```sh
ffmpeg -i input.mov \
  -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -preset medium \
  -c:a aac -b:a 192k \
  output.mp4
```

Adjust the quality and codec options to match the target device or sharing platform. Install FFmpeg using the [Kdenlive and FFmpeg setup](kdenlive.qmd).

## Audio conversion

Use FFmpeg to convert a WAV recording to MP3:

```sh
ffmpeg -i input.wav -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2 output.mp3
```

For a lossless FLAC output, use:

```sh
ffmpeg -i input.wav output.flac
```

FFmpeg chooses an encoder based on the output extension unless you specify one. Check playback and metadata after conversion, especially when preparing files for a specific device or service. See [Kdenlive and FFmpeg setup](kdenlive.qmd) for installation and [FFmpeg documentation](https://ffmpeg.org/documentation.html) for codec options.

## Cross-media conversion

Transcription converts the spoken audio in an audio or video recording to text. Use the local `transcribe` helper described in the [audio and video transcription guide](whisper.qmd). Video is used as an audio source; its visual content is not analyzed.
